Subject: TIA scoping: conditional processing carve-outs + subprocessor proof

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the quick follow-up on the DPA. We're running the APAC pilot and need to confirm a couple of operational items before legal signs off on the UK Addendum/TIA carve-outs. High-level asks: 

- Can Redwood confirm which subprocessors will handle ACK-encoded telemetry (EU/APAC) vs. pure inference logs?
- For processors that are multi-tenant GPUs, do you have a current certification or attestation (SOC2 or equivalent) we can accept as proof?
- We're trying to scope TIA appendix vs. DTIAs: if Redwood treats the platform as a processor and the customer data path touches regionally isolated nodes, do you have a formalized routing exception flow?

Attached is a draft scoping table (TIA_Scoping_Table_v0.3.xlsx) with our initial answers — most cells blank. Could you and Marissa mark columns for: subprocessors used, residency by region, and whether the subprocessor is covered by an independent certification? We need to produce a consolidated evidence package by EOD Friday (APAC).

Short call would help if possible — Aiden and I are flexible afternoon PST this week.

Thanks,
Samira

- Subprocessor mapping (owner: Marissa) — we'll populate the matrix with the current active pipeline: egress/ingest, KV-cache store, observability/telemetry, model cache. Expect an initial pass by EOD Wed.
- Certification/evidence (owner: Kimberly) — Kimberly will confirm which subprocessors provide SOC2 or ISO attestations and attach the latest PDFs. For third-party GPU hosting partners that don't publish SOC2, we'll provide an internal control matrix + access logs snapshot.
- Routing exception flow (owner: Priya) — Priya will confirm the documented routing exception (if a customer pins to region X, how we escalate to create a single-tenant carve-out or use a fallback compatible model).

Next steps:
1) Marissa to upload completed Annex-A subprocessor sheet to the Drive link and flag any subprocessors that require on-demand attestation.
2) Kimberly to attach processor certifications or control matrices.
3) Priya to summarize the routing exception steps and who to engage for private deployments.

If you prefer a call, I can set 30 minutes Wednesday 10:30–11:00 PST. Otherwise we'll push the deck and evidence to the Drive and confirm by Friday.

On Mon, Jun 30, 2025 at 11:08 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samira — thanks for the clear asks. Quick notes and proposed owners below. I added Priya for contractual context and Kimberly for infra/ops confirmation.

Thanks all — I did the first pass on the Annex-A matrix and uploaded it to the shared Drive (link below). Key callouts from the pass:

- Ingest: Veridian's regionally routed ingestion currently touches our edge transformer (partnered CDN) and then Dedicated inference pool. Subprocessor: EdgeCDN Ltd (edgecdn@example.com) — located APAC/EU/US. EdgeCDN publishes SOC2 Type II (cert attached).
- Model hosting: Redwood Dedicated pool (Redwood-managed infra) — not a third-party subprocessor; it's Redwood-managed. We'll annotate whether Dedicated is multi-tenant vs single-tenant for each customer.
- Telemetry/Observability: We use OpenObserv (third party) for aggregated telemetry; they provide an attestation but not SOC2. We can provide a control matrix and recent access logs as interim evidence.

I've attached a stamped evidence PDF for EdgeCDN and a lightweight "Proof_of_Processor_Certification.pdf" that bundles attestations we commonly share. For the ones lacking formal SOC2, Kimberly and infra will add the control matrix.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Marissa: finish Annex-A matrix and highlight 4 subprocessors lacking SOC2 (ETA: Wed EOD) — Attachment: DPA_AnnexA_Subprocessor_Matrix.xlsx
- Kimberly: provide control matrix and a sample access-log export for OpenObserv (ETA: Thu EOD)
- Priya: draft contract clause text for routing exceptions and single-tenant carve-outs (ETA: Thu)

Samira — can you confirm whether Veridian will accept the combination of an attestation + control matrix in lieu of SOC2 for non-SOC vendors for initial onboarding? We want to avoid re-running procurement unless necessary.

Regards,

Marissa — appreciate the tidy pass and the attachments. Quick answers: 

- Veridian can accept a certified attestation + control matrix for initial onboarding for up to 90 days if the vendor has a documented remediation plan and evidence of quarterly access reviews. After 90 days full SOC2/ISO proof is required or a formal waiver from our security council.
- For Dedicated single-tenant carve-outs we will need the routing exception flow documented and a contact list for escalation. A one-pager is sufficient.

I'll prepare a short acceptance note we can include in the DPA annex. Can we get Kimberly's OpenObserv control matrix by Thu EOD so our security team can do a fast-triage? If so, we can keep the onboarding timeline intact.

Call: Wed 17:00 PST works for me if you (Redwood) want to walk through the evidence rather than rely on the Drive.

Samira
